sara: Quick note — I ran a small bring-up for speculative decoding on quantized 13B (Q4_0) on raptor-8. Wanted to share raw observations before I file a formal runbook.
sara: Config: speculative candidate pool size 4, fast-path LM in int8, fallback full-decode in fp16 when entropy > 3.0.
sara: Short summary: latency median ~2.6x lower for interactive prompts, tail improved too; quality drop is measurable but small on automatic metrics (delta MMLU ≈ -0.7%, exact-match on SQuAD down ~0.9%).
kai: Nice. Can you paste the exact command you used to run the eval harness?
sara: Sure —
```
redwood-evals run --suite eval-suite:v2 \n  --model quant-13b-q4_0-spec --fallback-model fp16-13b \n  --speculative-candidates 4 --entropy-threshold 3.0 \n  --samples 2000 --tag raft-smoke
```
sara: This was a 2k sample quickpass on our english-heavy holdout.
jordan: Did you do pairwise A/B or absolute metric comparisons?
sara: Pairwise A/B vs fp16 baseline. We logged per-sample delta scores so we can compute sign tests. p-value is marginal for MMLU (p~0.04) but for SQuAD exact-match it's not significant on this sample. Need bigger N.
alex: Any qualitative failure modes? examples?
sara: A few cases where the fast-path returned slightly shorter/safer completions (cut off the reasoning chain). Also one reproducible hallucination pattern when the prefix had a rare entity — candidate beam all agreed on a plausible but wrong fact, fallback corrected it.
miguel: Interesting — that suggests uncertainty estimator is imperfect. Does entropy > 3.0 catch those?
sara: Not always. The hallucination example had moderate entropy but high KL divergence between candidates. We should experiment with a KL-based trigger in addition to entropy.

ci-bot: Smoke job jd-4821: tests passed (basic harness), artifacts uploaded to /artifacts/spec-decode/1879999999/
kai: Suggest measuring two additional signals: 1) candidate disagreement (pairwise BLEU/ROUGE or softmax-kl), 2) length ratio between fast-path top candidate and rescored fp16 output. Both are cheap.
sara: Agree. Also want to add a simple rescoring step: run fast-path candidates through a cheap fp16 rescorer (no full autoreg decode) and see improvement. Low-cost rescoring might recover most quality while keeping latency gains.
jordan: Please add a canary route in dedicated for 5% traffic so we get real-world latencies and error patterns. Also capture token-level logits for 1% of requests for offline analysis.
sara: Will do. Plan:
- expand sample N to 10k across multilingual holdouts
- add KL and length heuristics to fallback triggers
- run human evaluation on 1k paired samples for safety-sensitive prompts
- create canary 5% in dedicated and monitor rollout metrics (latency, fallback-rate, quality-delta)

alex: FYI we should quantify cost delta too — preliminary calc says per-token infra cost drops ~45% on fast-path, but fallback rescoring adds ~5% back. Net still good.
miguel: For regression detection, propose we add a paired-MAP threshold in the eval pipeline and block rollout if MMLU falls more than 1.0% and p<0.01. Also track rare-entity halluc rates.
sara: Good guardrails. I'll open a PR with the eval config and a JIRA for the canary rollout.

jordan: I'll draft the human eval instructions. Keep notes concise so we can ship the runbook. :thumbsup:
